text:
In the density measurement of a cube, the mass and
edge length are measured as (10.00 ± 0.10) kg and
(0.10 ± 0.01) m, respectively. The error in the
measurement of density is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$ρ=\frac{m}{l^{3}}=\frac{10.00}{(0.10)^{3}}=1.0\times 10^{4}\text{kg m}^{-3}$

$\frac{\Delta ρ}{ρ}=\frac{\Delta m}{m}+3\frac{\Delta l}{l}=\frac{0.10}{10.00}+3\times \frac{0.01}{0.10}=0.01+0.30=0.31$

The fractional error in the density is $0.31$, corresponding to an absolute error of $0.31\times 1.0\times 10^{4}=3.1\times 10^{3}\text{kg m}^{-3}$; the options quote the fractional error $0.31$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
An HCl molecule has rotational, translational
and vibrational motions. If the rms velocity of
HCl molecules in its gaseous phase is $v–$ , m is
its mass and $k_{B}$ is Boltzmann constant, then its
temperature will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The rms speed of a molecule is fixed by its translational kinetic energy alone, which by equipartition is $\dfrac{3}{2}k_{B}T$ per molecule irrespective of the rotational and vibrational modes:

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv–^{2}=\dfrac{3}{2}k_{B}T\Rightarrow T=\dfrac{mv–^{2}}{3k_{B}}.$

Rotational and vibrational energy add to the internal energy of the HCl molecule but do not change the speed of its centre of mass, so they do not enter this relation.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
A simple pendulum oscillating in air has period
T. The bob of the pendulum is completely
immersed in a non-viscous liquid. The density
of the liquid is
1/16 th of the material of the bob.
If the bob is inside liquid all the time, its period
of oscillation in this liquid is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a simple pendulum T = $2π\sqrt{\frac{L}{g_{err}}}$

Situation 1: when pendulum is in air $\to$ $g_{$eff} = g

Situation 2:when pendulum is in liquid

$\to$ $g_{$eff} = $\left (1-\frac{ρ_{liquid}}{ρ_{body}}\right )=g\left (1-\frac{1}{16}\right )=\frac{15g}{16}$

So, $\frac{T^{'}}{T}=\frac{2π\sqrt{\frac{L}{15g/16}}}{2π\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}}$

$\Rightarrow T^{{}^{'}}=\frac{4T}{\sqrt{15}}$

text:
The stream of a river is flowing with a speed
of 2km/h. A swimmer can swim at a speed of
4km/h. What should be the direction of the
swimmer with respect to the flow of the river to
cross the river straight ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The river flows at $2\text{km h}^{-1}$ and the swimmer's speed relative to the water is $4\text{km h}^{-1}$.

To cross straight, the swimmer's velocity relative to the ground must be perpendicular to the flow, so the swimmer must head upstream at an angle $θ$ from the perpendicular such that the upstream component cancels the river's velocity:

$4\sin θ=2\Rightarrow \sin θ=\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow θ=30^{\circ }$

The perpendicular makes $90^{\circ }$ with the direction of flow, and the heading is a further $30^{\circ }$ towards upstream, so the angle with the flow is $90^{\circ }+30^{\circ }=120^{\circ }$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

original speed. What is the mass of the second

By conservation of linear momentum:

$2v_{0}=2\left (\frac{v_{0}}{4}\right )+mv\Rightarrow 2v_{0}=\frac{v_{0}}{2}+mv$

$\Rightarrow \frac{3v_{0}}{2}=mv...(1)$

Since collision is elastic

$V_{separation}=V_{approach}$

$\Rightarrow v-\frac{v_{0}}{4}=v_{0}\Rightarrow m=\frac{6}{5}=1.2kg$

text:
The following bodies are made to roll up
(without slipping) the same inclined plane from
a horizontal plane. : (i) a ring of radius R, (ii)
a solid cylinder of radius
R/2 and (iii) a solid
sphere of radius
R/4 . If in each case, the speed
of the centre of mass at the bottom of the incline
is same, the ratio of the maximum heights they
climb is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Total kinetic energy of a rolling body is given as

$E_{\text{total}}=\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\left [1+\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}\right ]$

where, $K$ is the radius of gyration.

Using conservation law of energy,

$\begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\left [1+\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}\right ]=mgh \\  \\ \text{or}h=\frac{v^{2}}{2g}\left [1+\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}\right ] \end{array}$

For ring, $\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}=1$

$\Rightarrow h_{1}=\frac{v^{2}}{2g}[1+1]=\frac{2v^{2}}{2g}=\frac{v^{2}}{g}$

For solid cylinder, $\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}=\frac{(R/2\sqrt{2})^{2}}{(R/2)^{2}}$

$\begin{array}{ll} =\dfrac{R^{2}}{8}\times \dfrac{4}{R^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow h_{2} & =\dfrac{v^{2}}{2g}\left [1+\dfrac{1}{2}\right ]=\dfrac{3v^{2}}{4g} \end{array}$

For solid sphere, $\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}}=\frac{2}{5}$

$\Rightarrow h_{3}=\frac{v^{2}}{2g}\left [1+\frac{2}{5}\right ]=\frac{7v^{2}}{10g}$

So,the ratio of $h_{1},h_{2}$ and $h_{3}$ is

$\begin{array}{ll} h_{1}:h_{2}:h_{3} & =\dfrac{v^{2}}{g}:\dfrac{3v^{2}}{4g}:\dfrac{7}{10}\dfrac{v^{2}}{g} \\  \\ =1:\dfrac{3}{4}:\dfrac{7}{10}=20:15:14 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
A uniform cable of mass 'M' and length 'L' is
placed on a horizontal surface such that its $(1/n)^{th}$
part is hanging below the edge of the
surface. To lift the hanging part of the cable upto
the surface, the work done should be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we need to determine the work done to lift the hanging part of the cable up to the surface. The work done lifting a small element of the cable will be the weight of the element times the distance it has to be lifted.

Let's take a small section of the cable at a depth $x$ below the surface. This section has a length of $dx$, so its mass is $(M/L)dx$ where $(M/L)$ is the linear mass density of the cable.

The work $dW$ done to lift this small section up to the surface is the weight of the section times the distance it has to be lifted :

$dW=(M/L)gdx\times x$.

Integrating this expression from 0 to L/n (the length of the hanging part of the cable) gives the total work done :

$W=\int\limits _{0}^{L/n}(M/L)gxdx$

$=(Mg/L)\int\limits _{0}^{L/n}xdx$

$=(Mg/L)\times [x^{2}/2]_{0}^{L/n}$

$=(Mg/L)\times [L^{2}/(2n^{2})]$

$=MgL/(2n^{2})$

So the work done to lift the hanging part of the cable up to the surface is $MgL/(2n^{2})$.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C :

$\frac{MgL}{2n^{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot
